name: Technical explanation
intent: Correct, well-pitched technical prose for a named audience. Mixed on purpose: reading level and shape are rules, correctness and audience fit are judged, and the split is visible in the score method mix.

criteria.name: Pitched at the audience
criteria.intent: The audience is a working developer who has not seen this system. Grade 9-14 is what that means, numerically.

criteria.name: Explanatory shape
criteria.intent: An explanation has sections and at least one worked example. Both are countable.

criteria.name: Does not restate itself
criteria.intent: Padding an explanation by saying the same thing three ways is a measurable habit.

criteria.name: Technically correct
criteria.intent: The part no rule can carry: is what it says true.

descriptors.5: Every technical statement is correct, and the caveats are the right ones.
descriptors.4: Correct, with one imprecision that a reader would not be misled by.
descriptors.3: Broadly correct with one claim that is wrong in a way that matters.
descriptors.2: Several wrong claims, presented with the same confidence as the right ones.
descriptors.1: Confidently wrong about the central mechanism.

criteria.name: Fits its audience
criteria.intent: Assumes what a working developer knows, explains what they would not.

descriptors.5: Assumes exactly what a working developer knows; explains precisely what they would not.
descriptors.4: Well judged, with one term left undefined or one over-explained.
descriptors.3: Uneven: patronising in places, opaque in others.
descriptors.2: Consistently pitched at the wrong level.
descriptors.1: Unusable for this audience: either a glossary or a specification.
